"'''Lean on Me'''" is a song written and recorded by American singer-songwriter [[Bill Withers]]. It was released in April 1972 as the lead single from his second album, ''[[Still Bill]]''. It was a No. 1 single on both the soul and [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] charts, the latter chart for three weeks in July 1972.<ref>{{cite book |title= Top R&B/Hip-Hop Singles: 1942-2004|last=Whitburn |first=Joel |author-link=Joel Whitburn |year=2004 |publisher=Record Research |page=633}}</ref> ''Billboard'' ranked it as the No. 7 song of 1972.<ref>[[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1972]]</ref> 

Numerous other versions have been recorded, and it is one of only nine songs to have reached No. 1 on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 with versions recorded by two different artists with a 1987 cover by [[Club Nouveau]] also reaching No. 1.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Cover Me: Same Songs to Hit No. 1 By Two Different Artists|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/cover-me.shtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121228045014/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/cover-me.shtml|archive-date=December 28, 2012}}</ref> In 2007, the 1972 recording of the song by [[Bill Withers]] on [[Sussex Records]] was inducted into the [[Grammy Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=GRAMMY Hall Of Fame {{!}} Hall of Fame Artists |url=https://www.grammy.com/awards/hall-of-fame-award#l |access-date=September 14, 2024 |website=grammy.com}}</ref> It was ranked No. 208 on ''[[Rolling Stone]]''{{'}}s list of "[[The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time]]" in 2010.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/news/coverstory/500songs/page/3 |title=The RS 500 Greatest Songs of All Time : Rolling Stone |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=November 22, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080625061023/http://www.rollingstone.com/news/coverstory/500songs/page/3 |archive-date=June 25, 2008 }}</ref>

"Lean on Me" is a song written and recorded by American singer-songwriter Bill Withers. It was released in April 1972 as the lead single from his second album, Still Bill. It was a No. 1 single on both the soul and Billboard Hot 100 charts, the latter chart for three weeks in July 1972. Billboard ranked it as the No. 7 song of 1972. 

Numerous other versions have been recorded, and it is one of only nine songs to have reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 with versions recorded by two different artists with a 1987 cover by Club Nouveau also reaching No. 1. In 2007, the 1972 recording of the song by Bill Withers on Sussex Records was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame. It was ranked No. 208 on Rolling Stone{{'}}s list of "The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time" in 2010.

sections.heading: Background and writing
sections.wikitext:
Bill Withers's childhood in the coal mining town of [[Slab Fork, West Virginia]],{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/artists/billwithers/articles/story/6596050/lean_on_me |title=Lean on Me: Bill Withers : Rolling Stone |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=May 22, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071001175536/http://www.rollingstone.com/artists/billwithers/articles/story/6596050/lean_on_me |archive-date=October 1, 2007 }} was the inspiration for "Lean on Me", which he wrote for his album ''[[Still Bill]]'' after he had moved to [[Los Angeles]], and found himself missing the strong community ethic of his hometown. He had lived in a decrepit house in the poor section of his town. Withers recalled to [[Songfacts]] the original inspiration for the song:
"I bought a little piano and I was sitting there just running my fingers up and down the piano. In the course of doing the music, that phrase crossed my mind, so then you go back and say, 'OK, I like the way that phrase, Lean On Me, sounds with this song.'"{{cite web|url=http://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/bill_withers/ |title=Songfacts Interview with Bill Withers |website=Songfacts.com |access-date=2017-05-10}}
Withers stated in the same interview that he made an effort to keep the lyrics simple. Several members of the [[Charles Wright & the Watts 103rd Street Rhythm Band|Watts 103rd Street Rhythm Band]]Thompson, Dave (2001). "Charles Wright and the Watts 103rd Street Rhythm Band." Funk. San Francisco: Backbeat Books. pp. 203-206. were used for the recording session in 1972. A string section was also included.
sections.text:
Bill Withers's childhood in the coal mining town of Slab Fork, West Virginia, was the inspiration for "Lean on Me", which he wrote for his album Still Bill after he had moved to Los Angeles, and found himself missing the strong community ethic of his hometown. He had lived in a decrepit house in the poor section of his town. Withers recalled to Songfacts the original inspiration for the song:
"I bought a little piano and I was sitting there just running my fingers up and down the piano. In the course of doing the music, that phrase crossed my mind, so then you go back and say, 'OK, I like the way that phrase, Lean On Me, sounds with this song.'"
Withers stated in the same interview that he made an effort to keep the lyrics simple. Several members of the Watts 103rd Street Rhythm Band were used for the recording session in 1972. A string section was also included.

The [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]] group [[Club Nouveau]] covered the song with [[go-go]] beat on their album ''[[Life, Love & Pain]]'' and took it to No. 1 on [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart in March 1987.<ref name="clubnoveaucover">{{cite web|url={{BillboardURLbyName|artist=club nouveau|chart=all}}|title=Artist Chart History - Club Nouveau|publisher=Billboard Music Charts|access-date=June 6, 2009}}</ref> It also reached No. 1 on the [[Dance Club Songs|Dance Club Play]] chart<ref name="clubnoveaucover" /> and No. 2 on the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|Hot Black Singles]] chart. It won a [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Award]] in 1987 for Bill Withers, as the writer, for [[Grammy Award for Best R&B Song|Best R&B Song]] at the [[30th Annual Grammy Awards]].<ref name="clubnoveaugrammy">{{cite web|url=http://www.billwithersmusic.com/htmlWork/bio1.html |title=Bill Withers Biography |publisher=Billwithers.com |pages=8th Paragraph;Last Sentence |access-date=June 6, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110829182422/http://www.billwithersmusic.com/htmlWork/bio1.html |archive-date=August 29, 2011 }}</ref> The song ranked at No. 94 in [[VH1]]'s ''100 Greatest One-Hit Wonders of the 80s''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=VH1's 100 Greatest One Hit Wonders of the '80s: Do You Agree?|url=https://ew.com/article/2009/04/07/vh1s-100-greate/|website=EW.com|language=EN|access-date=May 7, 2020}}</ref>

The R&B group Club Nouveau covered the song with go-go beat on their album Life, Love & Pain and took it to No. 1 on Billboard Hot 100 chart in March 1987. It also reached No. 1 on the Dance Club Play chart and No. 2 on the Hot Black Singles chart. It won a Grammy Award in 1987 for Bill Withers, as the writer, for Best R&B Song at the 30th Annual Grammy Awards. The song ranked at No. 94 in VH1's 100 Greatest One-Hit Wonders of the 80s.

sections.heading: In popular culture
Notable cover versions
sections.wikitext:
In 1989, remakes of "Lean on Me" by [[the Winans]] and [[Sandra Reaves-Phillips]] provided the emotional uplift for the film ''[[Lean on Me (film)|Lean on Me]]''. For the same film, the song was adapted by [[Big Daddy Kane]] in "hip hop" form.<ref name="lommoviesongs">{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/dp/B000002LGP|title=Lean on Me: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack|website=Amazon|year=1989|access-date=June 6, 2009}}</ref>

In 1976, English [[glam rock]] band [[Mud (band)|Mud]] released their version which was a top 10 hit on both the [[UK singles chart]] and [[Irish Singles Chart|Irish singles chart]], peaking at No. 7 and No. 6, respectively.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/songs/mud-lean-on-me/|title=LEAN ON ME|date=November 27, 1976|website=Official Charts}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=The Irish Charts - All there is to know|url=https://www.irma.ie/search/%2A|website=irishcharts.ie}}</ref>

For the BBC's ''[[Children in Need]]'' in [[Children in Need 2016|2016]], 1,580 children in choirs sang the song in unison, live from nine towns across the UK.<ref name="CiN MK article">{{cite web|title=Milton Keynes pupils to perform live for bbc children in need|date=November 3, 2016 |url=https://www.miltonkeynes.co.uk/news/milton-keynes-pupils-to-perform-live-for-bbc-children-in-need-1183676}}</ref> The choirs started singing at the same time and on the telethon; starting in the studio it cut between the choirs giving them either one 20 second slot, or two 10 second slots on air before finishing in the studio. The choirs sang from [[Elstree]] at [[Elstree Studios]] (the studio just outside [[London]] where the main telethon was held),<ref name="CiN MK article"/> [[Liverpool]] at [[Sefton Park]],<ref name="CiN MK article"/> [[Swansea]] from [[Swansea University|The Swansea University Bay Campus]],<ref name="CiN MK article"/> [[Bridlington]] at [[Bridlington Spa]],<ref name="CiN MK article"/> [[Dudley]] at the [[Black Country Living Museum]],<ref name="CiN MK article"/> [[Glasgow]] at [[BBC Pacific Quay]],<ref name="CiN MK article"/> [[Milton Keynes]] at [[Stadium MK]],<ref name="CiN MK article"/> [[Salisbury]] at [[Salisbury Arts Centre]]<ref name="CiN MK article"/> and [[Belfast]] at [[Titanic Belfast|Titanic]].<ref name="CiN MK article"/>

In 2020, the song was recorded by an ad hoc [[Supergroup (music)|supergroup]] of Canadian musicians credited as ArtistsCAN, both in tribute to Withers' recent death and to raise funds for the [[Canadian Red Cross]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>Claire Shaffer, [https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/canada-lean-on-me-bill-withers-tribute-990242/ "Justin Bieber, Geddy Lee and More Sing ‘Lean on Me’ in Bill Withers Tribute"]. ''[[Rolling Stone]]'', April 27, 2020.</ref> Participating artists included [[Bryan Adams]], [[Jann Arden]], [[Justin Bieber]], [[Michael Bublé]], [[Fefe Dobson]], [[Scott Helman]], [[Shawn Hook]], [[Avril Lavigne]], [[Geddy Lee]], [[Marie-Mai]], [[Sarah McLachlan]], [[Johnny Orlando]], [[Josh Ramsay]], [[Buffy Sainte-Marie]], [[Tyler Shaw]], [[Walk Off the Earth]], [[Donovan Woods (musician)|Donovan Woods]], and Olivia Lunny.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kennedy |first=John R. |date=April 26, 2020 |title=Canadian Artists Join Voices For 'Lean On Me' |url=https://www.iheartradio.ca/news/canadian-artists-join-voices-for-lean-on-me-1.12227470 |access-date=January 6, 2021 |website=Iheartradio.ca |language=en-CA}}</ref>

In 2023, Japanese-American singer [[Ai (singer)|Ai]] performed the song live at the [[Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park]] during the [[49th G7 summit]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 21, 2023 |title=AI、G7広島サミット期間中の広島から＜Lasting Peace LIVE＞配信 |trans-title=Ai Broadcasts Lasting Peace LIVE from Hiroshima During the G7 Hiroshima Summit |url=https://www.barks.jp/news/?id=1000234311 |access-date=August 27, 2023 |website=BARKS |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 21, 2023 |title=AI、広島から世界へ平和へ願い G7サミット開催地で「アルデバラン」など大合唱 |trans-title=Ai prays for peace from Hiroshima to the world |url=https://www.oricon.co.jp/news/2279848/full/ |access-date=August 27, 2023 |website=Oricon}}</ref> Ai additionally covered "Lean on Me" during a surprise appearance at the G7's youth symposium that took place later the same day.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hiroshima Students Discuss Peace with the Spouses of G7 Leaders |url=https://unitar.org/about/news-stories/news/hiroshima-students-discuss-peace-spouses-g7-leaders |access-date=December 1, 2023 |website=UNITAR |language=en}}</ref> Her cover of "Lean on Me" later was included on her thirteenth studio album, ''[[Respect All]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 23, 2023 |title=【インタビュー】AI、アルバム『RESPECT ALL』にあなたへ届けたいメッセージ「もっと分かり合えたら」 |trans-title=(Interview) Ai wants to deliver a message on her album "Respect All" "If we could understand each other more" |url=https://www.barks.jp/news/?id=1000238761 |access-date=August 27, 2023 |website=Barks |language=ja}}</ref>
sections.text:
In 1989, remakes of "Lean on Me" by the Winans and Sandra Reaves-Phillips provided the emotional uplift for the film Lean on Me. For the same film, the song was adapted by Big Daddy Kane in "hip hop" form.

In 1976, English glam rock band Mud released their version which was a top 10 hit on both the UK singles chart and Irish singles chart, peaking at No. 7 and No. 6, respectively.

For the BBC's Children in Need in 2016, 1,580 children in choirs sang the song in unison, live from nine towns across the UK. The choirs started singing at the same time and on the telethon; starting in the studio it cut between the choirs giving them either one 20 second slot, or two 10 second slots on air before finishing in the studio. The choirs sang from Elstree at Elstree Studios (the studio just outside London where the main telethon was held), Liverpool at Sefton Park, Swansea from The Swansea University Bay Campus, Bridlington at Bridlington Spa, Dudley at the Black Country Living Museum, Glasgow at BBC Pacific Quay, Milton Keynes at Stadium MK, Salisbury at Salisbury Arts Centre and Belfast at Titanic.

In 2020, the song was recorded by an ad hoc supergroup of Canadian musicians credited as ArtistsCAN, both in tribute to Withers' recent death and to raise funds for the Canadian Red Cross during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participating artists included Bryan Adams, Jann Arden, Justin Bieber, Michael Bublé, Fefe Dobson, Scott Helman, Shawn Hook, Avril Lavigne, Geddy Lee, Marie-Mai, Sarah McLachlan, Johnny Orlando, Josh Ramsay, Buffy Sainte-Marie, Tyler Shaw, Walk Off the Earth, Donovan Woods, and Olivia Lunny.

In 2023, Japanese-American singer Ai performed the song live at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park during the 49th G7 summit. Ai additionally covered "Lean on Me" during a surprise appearance at the G7's youth symposium that took place later the same day. Her cover of "Lean on Me" later was included on her thirteenth studio album, Respect All.
